myths.title: Name and Meaning
myths.text: The name means "Creator of the earth; primordial ancestor of the Yoruba" and reflects the figure's role in the tradition.

lore.syncretism: Odùduwà appears within the Yoruba tradition and has influenced later retellings, artistic depictions, and scholarly study. The Unicode restoration preserves the name's distinctive orthography for contemporary use.
lore.culturalLegacy: Odùduwà continues to appear in scholarship, art, and popular reception as a significant figure of the Yoruba tradition. Restoring the name in Unicode returns the original marks that ASCII removes.
lore.extendedMeditation: Odùduwà embodies progenitor, ile-ife, first king in the Yoruba imagination. The name's restoration is not merely cosmetic: it recovers the stress, length, and script that make the figure recognizable in the source tradition.
lore.archaeology: Odùduwà is attested in the textual and iconographic record of the Yoruba tradition.
